params.body:
## What Shane saw

On a phone (390 px) the edit sheet of a VW T-Roc opened with the title over two lines, three full-width buttons stacked (Acties, Bekijken, overzicht), a grey status block of four rows, and only then the step indicator "2 van 8, Algemeen". The first field was below the fold. On the same sheet the description textareas read larger and heavier than their label, and the numeric fields with a unit (kg, mm, €) stopped at about 60% of the width with the number hanging mid-screen, showing `1860.00` and `225.72` on a screen that writes `200.000` km.

## The header (X-127, R S1-9.18)

**The three buttons become one row.** The back link is a 44 px square with only the arrow (its word is hidden, `aria-label` keeps the name), Bekijken and Acties share the rest as two equal columns (a grid with `minmax(0, 1fr)` twice: two flex items with basis 0 still came out 136 and 158 px wide, and two unequal buttons read as a hierarchy that is not there). Back sits left, as on every phone screen; Acties sits right, where the ⋯ menu of a vehicle card also sits. **Nothing is folded into the menu**: the way back is the most frequent tap and a menu would cost it a second one; Bekijken is a link to what the customer sees, not a document; and the menu stays what it is, the list of documents (offer, order, test drive). On a phone the Acties menu opens as a bottom sheet, the same sheet as the list header menus of PR 343 and the card's ⋯ menu: dark layer behind it (`::before` of the group, closed by `@click.self`), 50 px rows, Annuleren at the bottom, caret driven by `aria-expanded`. A draft (no menu, no Bekijken) gets one wide column for the chassis lookup next to the arrow (`:not(:has(.ui-head-menu))`).

**The status block becomes one row that may wrap.** Label then switch, no 1.2x scale, the switch box exactly its 44 px track (the list gave it 30 px of padding under a track drawn at -56 px, which ran over the label). The publish state and its button sit right, on a second line when the first is full. The word STATUS says nothing the labels do not and is hidden on a phone; in optie, klaar voor keuring and Op Stocklist stay readable at a glance. The switches stay where they were (the Data step binds `technical_ready` too, "In optie" is a modal flow with no field home), so nothing moves and nothing is lost.

**The title** is 18 px on a phone; a long name still wraps.

Measured at 390×844: step indicator from 434 px to 261 px, first field from about 590 px to 417 px, status block from 155 px to 72 px. The stepper header, its dots and the Vorige/Volgende/Opslaan grid at 480 px are untouched and still follow the shorter header. Desktop: the header region of the 1440 px screenshot is pixel-identical before and after (`ImageChops.difference` bbox starts at y=391, inside the form body).

## The fields (X-128, X-129, R S1-3.20, R S1-3.21)

**Textareas.** The two description boxes carry `ui-input` like every field, but a rule for screens under 480 px set `.ui-edit textarea.ui-input` to 16 px (against the iOS zoom on a field under 16 px) while inputs and selects stayed at 14 px; the colour was already the same brand ink, the size difference read as weight. The rule keeps its 180 px height and loses the font size. A second, older rule (`.ui-edit textarea`, `.ui-edit select`) gave textareas and selects the fainter line border instead of the field border of `.ui-input`; both now exclude `.ui-input`. Same fix covers the condition and remark textareas on Overig and the damage notes. The autogrow (`uiAutogrow`) sets only `height` and `overflow-y` inline and does not fight the stylesheet. The iOS zoom is a separate decision that applies to all fields or none; noted in X-128. The offer/order modals are outside `.ui-edit` and were never affected.

**Numeric fields with a unit.** Decision 1, alignment: right-aligned numbers stay right-aligned; the 220 px cap on `.ui-affix` with a unit span (and on the date boxes) is a desktop rule and is lifted under 768 px, so the field takes the full width like every other and the number sits at the edge of the form. Desktop keeps the 220 px.

Decision 2, format, per field:
- **weight, loaded_weight** (kg, `double`): whole and grouped like the kilometre boxes, `1.860` (`Custom::quantityInput`); a stored fraction, which nothing produces in practice (VWE delivers whole kilograms), keeps two decimals `1.860,50` so the display never rounds a value away.
- **road_tax_*, registration_tax_*** (€, `double`): comma and two decimals, `225,72` (`Custom::decimalInput`), no grouping, like the price boxes.
- **width, height, length** (`int`): were already whole; unchanged.
- **Parsing**: `OwnStockService::normaliseDecimals` (part of `normaliseAmounts`, so both doors pass through it before validation and before the write) reads `1.860`, `1860`, `1860,5`, `225,72` and `225.72` as the same number; the Livewire draft save takes the same road. The taxes were never parsed on either door until now (a comma would have reached the double column as a string). What is stored does not change.
- **Not touched**: the price boxes still show `27500.00`; their classic submit handler and the offer/order JS read a point-decimal, so they move as one later. Recorded in X-129.

**Finding, not changed**: `width`, `height`, `length` are `int NULL DEFAULT 0`. A vehicle without dimensions carries `0`, the sheet shows `0`, and the transport calculation (R S1-3.11) reads that 0 as a measurement. Whether 0 stands for "unknown" is a question for Ilse; recorded in X-129 without changing semantics.

## Tests

`tests/Feature/VehicleSheetHeaderTest` renders the real edit page with `actingAsWithRights($user, 'ownvehicle')` on both doors: one action row with back (with `aria-label`), Bekijken and the menu (`@click.self`, `aria-haspopup`, `:aria-expanded`), the step indicator present, a draft without menu or Bekijken; weights and taxes reading Dutch on both doors, `normaliseAmounts` reading them back, and a Livewire save storing 1860 / 225.72 / 310.45 from `1.860` / `225,72` / `310,45`; every textarea a `ui-input` and no own font size for textareas in the stylesheet. `StylesheetSyntaxTest` green (new classes `ui-head-actions`, `ui-head-menu`, `ui-head-view`, `ui-head-back`, `ui-head-back-label`).

`vendor/bin/phpunit --filter='VehicleForm|OwnStock|StylesheetSyntax|AlpineExpression|RulesCoverage|VehicleSheet|RulesDocsBuild'`: OK (83 tests, 1177 assertions), on a database from `mysql-schema.sql` plus the post-2026-07-28 migrations.

## Docs

R S1-9.18 (header on a phone), R S1-3.20 (one type size and colour for every field, full width under 768 px), R S1-3.21 (weights and taxes read Dutch, parsed tolerantly, stored unchanged); findings X-127, X-128, X-129 (renumbered after X-126 landed on main tonight).
params.title: The vehicle sheet's header and fields fit a phone
